Rationale.GT1_ModelGeneralization: The concept lens finding generalizes to Meta-Llama-3-8B. On capital cities task, concept lens (22%) significantly outperformed raw hidden states (6%), showing a 16% absolute improvement. While absolute performance is lower than on Llama-2-7b, the qualitative finding that concept induction heads improve semantic parallelogram arithmetic holds on the new model.
Rationale.GT2_DataGeneralization: The finding generalizes to completely new data instances. On 20 new capital-country pairs (Dublin-Ireland, Warsaw-Poland, Prague-Czechia, Vienna-Austria, etc.) with NO overlap with original dataset, concept lens achieved 60% accuracy while raw hidden states achieved 0%. This strongly validates that the method identifies a genuine semantic subspace, not memorized patterns.
Rationale.GT3_MethodGeneralization: The method generalizes to new task types not used in main experiments. On currency task (semantic): concept lens (8%) > raw (0%). On plural task (grammatical): token lens (60%) > concept (30%) > raw (14%). The task-type to lens-type mapping from the paper (concept for semantic, token for grammatical) correctly predicts which lens type works best on new tasks.
